Note::collapse_spaces¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::collapse_spaces() const

Fold Runs Of Spaces And Tabs To One Space¶

collapse_spaces() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with every run of one or more spaces or tabs in each cell replaced by a single space. Newlines and carriage returns are not touched, and the cell is not trimmed — so multi-line layout and any leading indent survive.

This is the narrower cousin of collapse_whitespace: use collapse_spaces when you want to normalise horizontal spacing inside lines while keeping the line structure, and collapse_whitespace when the whole thing should become one trimmed line.

collapse_spaces changes only horizontal spacing; letters, punctuation, and non-ASCII are untouched. It is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note.

Example 1: A Batch¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"a   b     c", "keep\nthe\nnewlines"}).collapse_spaces())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["a b c", "keep\nthe\nnewlines"]

The multi-space runs in the first cell collapse; the newlines in the second are left alone.

See Also¶

  • Note::collapse_whitespace: also folds newlines and trims the edges.

  • Note::collapse_newlines: the vertical counterpart.

  • Note::strip: trim the edges only.
